title: Callout annotator and shift-boundary playbook coverage mapper
author: Lucas Ramirez
release_notes: Adds a callout annotation pipeline and a playbook coverage mapper. New CLI: `slo-toolkit playbook-coverage`. Backfill job included. No breaking changes.
description:
Motivation: On-call responders frequently get paged with terse callouts; understanding which sections of a playbook are actually actionable during a responder's shift boundary is a recurring source of friction. This PR introduces two complementary pieces: (1) a lightweight callout annotator that enriches incoming alerts/pager callouts with contextual runbook fragments and signal-level hints, and (2) a shift-boundary playbook coverage mapper that computes which playbook playlets have owners for upcoming shifts and surfaces coverage gaps to the on-call UI and CLI.

What this changes (summary):
- New service `callout-annotator` (go) that subscribes to alert stream (Kafka topic `alerts.enriched`) and attaches: runbook fragment IDs, confidence hints, quick remediation snippets, and suggested escalation paths. It stores annotations to the existing `telemetry_annotations` table (nullable columns so non-breaking).
- New mapper job `playbook-coverage-mapper` (python) that scans playbook metadata, on-call rotation schedules (PagerDuty/SCIM import), and computes per-shift coverage vectors. Mapper writes a compact coverage manifest (S3 prefix) consumed by console and CLI.
- CLI command: `slo-toolkit playbook-coverage --shift YYYY-MM-DDTHH` that prints coverage heatmap and open responsibilities.
- Console integration: a new badge in the on-call incident panel that links to the coverage manifest and shows missing owners for recommended playlets. (Frontend change limited to a small badge and link).
- Backfill: one-off job to generate coverage manifests for the last 30 days (included as `scripts/coverage_backfill.py`).

Checklist: 
- [x] API and storage schema changes are additive and backward compatible (new nullable fields).
- [x] Unit tests for annotator matching heuristics and mapper logic (coverage thresholds, owner lookup).
- [x] E2E smoke: local runner that replays sample alerts and verifies annotation writes + coverage manifest output.
- [x] Load test: annotator processed 2k alerts/s in bench harness with 50ms median per-message processing.
- [x] Docs: developer notes, CLI usage, and an ops runbook for rollout and rollback.

Design notes and tradeoffs:
- We intentionally keep annotation payloads small (IDs + short strings) to avoid duplicating large runbook content across the telemetry store. The annotator references canonical playlet IDs which the console expands lazily.
- Coverage mapping happens at shift granularity (4 hour windows by default) to keep manifest size bounded; we can later add per-minute slices if needed.
- The annotator uses a heuristic matcher (name + regex + entropy-based fingerprint) rather than a heavy ML model to keep runtime and infra cost down; accuracy is ~84% on internal eval set.

Commits summary: 
- Initial annotator service and message consumer (go): callout-annotator/main.go + matching logic + unit tests.
- Playbook coverage mapper (python): mapper, serializer to S3, and backfill script.
- CLI: add `playbook-coverage` subcommand and small output formatter.
- Console: add coverage badge and fetcher client.
- infra: IAM role for mapper S3 writes, new k8s cronjob, helm chart additions.

Changed areas (high level list):
- services/callout-annotator/* (new)
- tools/playbook-coverage/* (new)
- web/console/src/components/OncallBadge.tsx (small change)
- cli/slo-toolkit/coverage.py (new)
- infra/helm/templates/callout-annotator.yaml (new)
- infra/iam/roles.yaml (small addition)
- scripts/coverage_backfill.py (new)

CI and test summary: 
- CI run 1: unit tests (go/python), linter, build: PASS.
- CI run 2: integration smoke against staging cluster: PASS (annotator wrote to telemetry_annotations staging table).
- Bench job: local bench harness measured 2k alerts/s peak; median processing time 50ms.

Rollout plan: 
1) Deploy annotator to staging, monitor latency and annotation correctness for 24 hours (staging flag enabled).
2) Deploy coverage-mapper as cronjob in staging; generate manifests and validate UI/CLI consumption.
3) Canary deploy annotator in production to 10% of alert traffic (routing rule feature flag).
4) If stable after 48 hours, increase to 50% then full.
5) Run backfill after full rollout to populate historical manifests.

Migration notes: DB changes are additive; scripts included to backfill existing alerts with annotation keys. To rollback remove feature flag to stop traffic and remove k8s deployment; S3 manifests are idempotent and can be deleted if needed.

Security considerations: annotations do not include PII or full alert payloads. We run a sanitizer step to scrub any user-provided text before saving. IAM policy scope is minimized to specific S3 prefix and telemetry_annotations table.

Related work: builds on ENG-1289 (playbook metadata normalization) and SRE-447 (oncall rotation importer).

Note: the description is intentionally compact; unit and integration tests are in the PR for reviewers to run locally.
